name: Vantablack Operations Thermal Coat
description:
A long insulated coat issued to Vantablack field personnel operating in cold-weather or extended outdoor conditions. The shell is a matte charcoal ripstop with a subtle corponation identifier woven into the collar lining — not a logo, just a thread pattern that reads under UV. Filled with a thin but highly effective synthetic insulation, the coat is warm without the bulk that would restrict movement or make it harder to access sidearms or equipment. Two deep hand pockets, a zippered chest pocket, and a sealed interior document pocket.

This coat signals Vantablack in a way that the average person recognizes without being able to articulate why. It's not branded. It's just cut a certain way, in a certain color, with a certain quality of fabric, worn by people who move with a certain economy. On the Shelf, seeing this coat means getting out of the way. In Tier 4 corridors, it means a meeting is happening that you're not part of.
functionality: Integrated front ballistic liner rated for standard rounds. UV-reactive thread identifier in collar lining for field recognition.
what_it_says: You work for Vantablack in a capacity that requires being outdoors for long periods, which means whatever you're doing is serious.
worn_by: corporate security contractors on outdoor assignment
anyone who's acquired one through unofficial channels and is either very brave or very stupid
story_hooks: A Vantablack Operations Thermal Coat shows up in a Shelf secondhand market — Vantablack does not sell surplus, which means someone stripped it off a body or stole it from supply.
The UV-reactive identifier in this coat's collar is from a discontinued field unit — wearing it suggests either a very old coat or a very deep cover.
A contact reaches out wearing one of these coats but claims to have no affiliation with Vantablack — they want help and they won't explain the coat.
